identification.title: Only a Holy God
identification.notes: Written by Michael Farren, Rich Thompson, Dustin Smith and Jonny Robinson; copyright 2016 Farren Love And War Publishing, Integrity's Alleluia! Music, Integrity's Praise! Music, Jonny Robinson, Rich Thompson and CityAlight Music, administered by Integrity Music; CCLI 7073332; original key D per PraiseCharts. The list's guess of CityAlight is right for the recording churches know. Reviewed as the song, not as any one recording.

claims.structuralNotes: Three verses built on rhetorical questions, each answered by the same short line, a chorus calling the congregation to behold and worship, and a closing repeat. The first verse concerns God's authority over heaven and kings; the second his beauty, majesty and justice; the third his glory, his power to raise the dead and his undefeated name. A final verse turns personal: God rescues the singer from failure, gave his Son, and invites the singer to call him Father. The chorus is a corporate exhortation, the verses declare, and the last verse is personal. The song is built on Isaiah 6, Psalm 96, Revelation 4, Romans 8 and John 3:16. The Spirit and the church are not named.

claims.claim: God holds authority over heaven and over earthly kings.
claims.subject: The sovereignty of God

claims.claim: God is beautiful, majestic and just, and only he is worthy of such praise.

claims.claim: God's glory and power reach to raising the dead, and his name has never been defeated.

strengths.title: Holiness set beside majesty and justice
strengths.explanation: Verses name God's authority, beauty, majesty, justice and glory, so worship is anchored in who he is before anything is asked or felt.
strengths.scriptureRationale: The holiness of God that fills the earth with glory.

strengths.title: Kings and heaven under one rule
strengths.explanation: The questions put heaven and earthly rulers under God's authority and the answer is always the same, so the claim is learned by repetition.
strengths.scriptureRationale: The Lord is great and to be feared above all gods.

strengths.title: Power to raise the dead and an undefeated name
strengths.explanation: The third verse ties God's glory to his power over death and to the name above every name.
strengths.scriptureRationale: The name given to Christ before which every knee bows.

strengths.title: The holy God invites us to call him Father
strengths.explanation: The final verse moves from rescue and the giving of the Son to access as a child, which is the gospel's own order of rescue then relationship.
strengths.scriptureRationale: The Spirit of adoption by whom we cry Abba, Father.

doctrinesAffirmed: The holiness and majesty of God
theological.assessment: Nothing to correct. The song is a sustained declaration of God's holiness and rule, built on Isaiah 6 and Revelation 4, that turns at the end to rescue, the giving of the Son and adoption. The cross and resurrection are alluded to rather than told, and the Spirit is not named.

strengths.title: A question and answer pattern that teaches itself
strengths.explanation: The repeated question, answered by one short line, is learned within a verse and invites the room to answer together.

strengths.title: The chorus calls the room to worship
strengths.explanation: The chorus addresses the congregation rather than the singer's feelings, which suits gathered singing.

communal.vocalRangeNote: Published with D as the original key per PraiseCharts. Test the chorus with the congregation before settling a key.

range.note: No chart was read for this review, so the pitches are not stated.

communal.repetitionAssessment: The chorus returns several times, and the repeated answer line reinforces the claim being made rather than filling time.
communal.assessment: Congregational in words and form. The pattern is easy to learn and the chorus speaks to the room, so it works as a call to worship or an opening song.

strengths.title: God is the subject throughout
strengths.explanation: Each verse is about God and his attributes, so the congregation knows whom it addresses and why.

clarity.assessment: Clear in its claims. The cross and resurrection are not narrated, so a visitor learns who God is more fully than how sinners are saved, until the final verse.

synthesis.summary: A declaration of God's holiness, authority, beauty and power over death, built on Isaiah 6 and Revelation 4, with a congregational chorus calling the room to behold and worship. A final verse turns to rescue, the giving of the Son and adoption. Nothing in it is wrong; the cross itself is not narrated. No independent assessment of its content was found.
